newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain asks France to protect produce importers.
newsitem.headline: Spain asks France to protect produce importers.

text.p: Spain has asked France to protect Spanish truckers after French farmers dumped and burned loads of imported fruits and vegetables this week, an official said on Friday.
The Foreign Ministry protested to the French ambassador in Spain on Thursday after an incident in Marseille involving three trucks, government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters.
Spain asked the French government to ensure that police acted more quickly to prevent such vandalism and to reimburse Spanish importers for any losses, Rodriguez said.

A leading Spanish agricultural association, ASAJA, called on Friday for a boycott of all French goods to protest against the destruction of fruit and vegetable imports to France. It said such attacks had been going on for years with impunity.
"ASAJA calls on the Spanish society to stop consuming all types of products of French origin," the group said in a statement.
ASAJA said it had sent a written appeal to the major Spanish supermarkets to stop selling French goods.
Spanish newspaper reports on Friday said French gendarmes had stood by while farmers, demanding tighter controls on cheap imported produce, dumped the Spanish vegetables and fruits.
ASAJA denounced what it called the "passivity and permissiveness of the (French) authorities".
Spanish Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio on Thursday accused the French government of neglecting its duties.
"It (the government) must guarantee free access of Spanish products to its markets," she said.
ASAJA said the Spanish agriculture sector had lost billions of 10 pesetas and market share due to vandalism in France. It demanded free circulation be guaranteed under European convergence.
